newsitem.title: USA: N.American pork producers seek open Taiwan markets.
newsitem.headline: N.American pork producers seek open Taiwan markets.

text.p: North American pork producers on Friday called on Taiwan to open its markets for pork imports, with the island's own hog herd devastated by an outbreak of foot and mouth disease.

The U.S.-based National Pork Producers Council (NPPC) hosted a meeting in Chicago with officials of the Canadian Pork Council, the Mexican Pork Council and the Mexico-based National Commission for Pork Products (CONAPOR).
"North American producers have had to open their markets, so we believe Taiwanese producers should do the same," CONAPOR president Antonia Canaan said in a statement.
Taiwan currently has an import ban on pork variety meats, such as stomachs, feet and tongues, and selectively restricts other cuts of pork such as bellies, the statement, issued by the NPPC, said.
The meeting coincided with a meeting between U.S. and Taiwan negotiators in Taipei concerning Taiwan's accession to the World Trade Organization.
